method.browser: isolated scripted Firefox 153.0.4 and Chrome 153 desktop sessions
method.native: Linux native release under isolated Xvfb sessions
limitations: Persona satisfaction is a task-completion proxy, not measured user sentiment.
Keyboard simulation is not screen-reader or assistive-technology validation.
No production calibration dataset or fab-wide accuracy claim was evaluated.

evidence: An isolated Firefox/WASM run immediately showed Gross 767, Yield 92.36%, Expected Good approximately 708, and separate explanations of geometry and random loss.
The selected 300 mm (12 in) preset, Diameter (12 in) field, and map badge using the diameter symbol all agreed that the input is nominal wafer diameter.
Character-by-character entry retained 10.123456 mm and changed Gross from 767 to an independently enumerated 753 and Expected Good to approximately 695.
Keyboard interaction selected Poisson and updated the model selector and disclosure title without changing the geometric Gross result.
The isolated novice automation selected Poisson but stopped with the selector open before capturing its formula disclosure; the separate expert run verified that model-specific formulas are exposed.
An independent corner-fit enumerator reproduced Gross 767 from 10.12 by 8.12 mm pitch and 147 mm usable radius; the UI separately reported 124 partial and 40 edge-band sites.
Independent exposure 0.08 and Murphy result 0.923608780147 matched the exact export; Poisson, Murphy, Seeds, and negative-binomial formulas and parameters were exposed.

The 2,031-byte JSON report identified schema v1, calculator 0.2.0, geometry method v1, normalized inputs, exact values, boundary, pitch, radial, notch, area, phase, rounding, and illustrative-map policies.
Fresh native and browser exports were byte-identical for JSON and SVG, and both displayed Gross 767, Murphy 92.36%, and expected good approximately 708.
All 12 validator tests passed, including refusal below 12 projects, coefficient withholding, ambiguous-count, unit, area-bound, grouped-holdout, and shared-source attacks.
An independent Trunk 0.21.14 release build reproduced the frozen index, JavaScript, and WASM hashes exactly.
Independent grid and analytic oracles reproduced Gross, boundary counts, four formulas, zero and high-exposure limits, monotonicity, and model identities.
Invalid values, last-valid state, no-Tab recovery, Reset, tangencies, asymmetric scribes, whole-pitch phases, and the grid-allocation guard passed.
An 11-project candidate returned no recommendation and no coefficients; 150 mm diameter area bounds, units, target semantics, source reuse, and grouped LOPO attacks were rejected.
The repository, UI, reports, scripts, skill, and workflows contain no supplied product, customer, or foundry identity and make no real-user or fitted-production claim.

personas.label: Keyboard user on a constrained viewport

evidence: At 500 by 1000 the order was result summary, Calculation setup, then Wafer map.
Tab showed a visible Report focus ring, Enter opened the report, and Escape returned to the main view.
Keyboard navigation selected the 76 mm preset and updated the result summary.
A 40 mm edge-exclusion error retained the last result, and replacing it with 3 without Tab cleared the error and restored Gross 31 and Expected Good approximately 29.
Scripted inter-key delay retained the full visible 10.123456 value rather than synchronizing over the active edit buffer.
Independent active-rectangle enumeration produced Gross 767, partial 124, and edge-band 40 for the default 300 mm geometry.
At unit exposure the implementation and independent analytic values matched for Poisson, Murphy triangular, Seeds, and negative binomial alpha 2.
Zero, near-zero, high exposure, monotonicity, negative-binomial alpha 1 equals Seeds, and large-alpha convergence to Poisson passed.
80 mm2 converted to 0.8 cm2 and exposure 0.08; Murphy yield and exact expectation 708.4079343726257 matched high-precision references.
A one-Gross Poisson fixture at D0 ln(2) yielded exact 0.5, rounded good 1, and displayed defective 0.
Non-finite and range errors, invalid clustering alpha, dense-grid guard, high exposure, and near-radius exclusion were handled without invalid results.
Whole-pitch equivalence, half-pitch change, asymmetric scribes, exact tangencies, partial-boundary, and edge-band cases matched independent geometry.
Invalid edits retained clearly marked last-valid results and blocked export; no-Tab recovery and Reset returned consistent current results.
Whole-pitch-equivalent offsets emitted identical JSON and SVG with canonical normalized phases.

Fresh native and browser JSON hashes both equal 65b0116747ece91b15fc02a83ccfd29b4a8b297f4a2208f1b9e8a7a22630ba30; SVG hashes both equal 00103844f830d4013678f3986932fce0cf88722a83495353674864d55b983db4.
A reported 2,882 dies at 150 mm diameter exceeded the physical area bound; redundant area, dimension basis, and scribe units were also checked.
Yield-adjusted targets, ambiguous counts, pre-shrink dimensions, wrong shape policy, non-opaque identifiers, reused sources, and grouped holdout leakage were rejected.
The default minimum is 12 independent project/source groups; an 11-project candidate emitted no recommendation and null coefficients.

findings.summary: Scenario comparison has no retained baseline or explicit delta
evidence: Deterministic JSON allows manual comparison, but the current application does not retain two named scenarios side by side.

findings.summary: The supplied 150 mm wafer label was physically incompatible with the reported Gross counts
evidence: The validator rejects the counts at 150 mm diameter, the application consistently labels nominal diameter, and no coefficient was fitted from the ambiguous records.

findings.summary: One-decimal yield values were incorrectly treated as proof of a Poisson model
evidence: Poisson and Murphy round to the same displayed examples; the application now names the selected model and exposes its formula and exact values.

findings.summary: The README screenshot showed the obsolete four-card workspace
evidence: The new 1600x900 attachment preserves the old left-workspace/right-report composition, matches the current v0.2.0 UI, and keeps the old attachment in Issue 1.
